title: FastProof tactical battlegrid + seller ops notes (draft)
body:
Purpose: quick, actionable battlegrid + seller-facing ops cheat notes for pilot and field troubleshooting. Very tactical — designed for SEs and platform sellers to run a 30–90 day pilot and handle the top 6 objections without dragging in infra.

High-level intent
- Short deck (8 slides) that an SE can run in a 10–12 minute demo + 5m Q&A.
- Battlegrid is a one-page visual used in call to align on tradeoffs: latency vs unit-cost vs reliability.
- Talk track templates + roleplay snippets for common friction points (privacy, SLA, fallback, noisy outputs).

Slide outline (minimal, to convert to slides)
1) 30s opener: Why inference economics matter now
   - 2 bullets: predictable unit cost = product velocity; graceful degradation = user trust
   - One line: Redwood approach = "Serve-first" (runtime + ops rules)
2) Starter config for pilots (3-step)
   - Quick checklist: model choice + caching strategy + route policy
   - Typical pilot size: 1M tokens/month projected -> recommended reserved pool: 2 GPUs (dedicated) or hosted with burst
3) Battlegrid visual (single slide)
   - X axis: latency sensitivity (low -> high)
   - Y axis: cost sensitivity (low -> high)
   - Overlay: reliability band (green/orange/red), suggested modes (hosted, dedicated, private)
   - Callout: "If in upper-right (high latency + high cost-sensitivity) -> suggest quantized smaller model + prefix caching"
4) Top 6 objections + 20s answers (battlecard style)
   - Data residency: offer Private (VPC/on-prem) + KMS/HSM notes
   - Latency: show 95th pct numbers, fallback flow, warm KV cache importance
   - Cost: model-family vs quantization tradeoff, batching heuristics
   - Reliability: model variants + multi-region fallback policies
   - Integration friction: SDK quickstart + infra diagram link
   - Security/compliance: audit logs + enterprise support cadence
5) Live demo plan (3 min)
   - Warm path: show short prompt -> streaming gen -> tool call example
   - Surge scenario: simulate burst and demonstrate fallback to cheaper model
6) Pilot KPIs + instrumentation
   - Primary: 95th latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate (model/infra)
   - Secondary: usage growth, cache hit rate, token/prompt distribution
   - Instrumentation hooks: trace id example, route metrics, per-token cost breakdown
7) Playbook: common runbooks (ops)
   - Canary rollback steps (3 commands or Console clicks)
   - How to enable KV caching and verify hit rate
   - Emergency fallback: switch route policy -> small-model fallback -> notify customer
8) Next steps + commitment ask
   - 2-week pilot start, internal kickoff, daily 15m first week
   - Ask: pilot commitment (data samples + contact on infra)

Battlegrid (content, to render visually)
- Use discrete zones with sample customer personas pinned:
  - Zone A (Low latency, low cost sensitivity): Hosted, large model, no dedicated
  - Zone B (High latency, low cost sensitivity): Dedicated with fast GPUs
  - Zone C (Low latency, high cost sensitivity): Quantized model + aggressive caching
  - Zone D (High latency, high cost sensitivity): Private deployment + predictive batching
- Quick heuristic: If 95p latency target < 350ms -> consider dedicated or private. If cost/mo > $50k -> reserved capacity + Optimize runbook.

One-pagers / Battlecard snippets (copyable into Slack)
- "If CFO asks about cost predictability: we recommend a reserved capacity trial (monthly commit) + per-route budgeting; we provide token-level cost breakdowns and caching suggestions to cut per-token spend by 30–70% depending on prompt reuse."
- "If infra team worries about failover: we run automatic model fallback + regional routing with health probes; can provide runbook for failover test."

Roleplay snippets (SE <-> Buyer)
- Buyer: "We can't risk exposing customer data"
  SE: "We can run the pilot in your VPC or on-prem; we integrate with your KMS and ship audit logs daily — I can set up a short security review with our security team this week."
- Buyer: "Latency spikes worry us"
  SE: "Quick mitigation path: enable prefix/KV caching and a small-model fallback; warm cache with a synthetic trace and verify 95th latency on the dashboard together."

Operational runbooks (compact)
- Canary rollback (Console): 1) Open rollout page -> 2) Select canary -> 3) Rollback to previous stable -> 4) Confirm traffic drain
- Emergency fallback (CLI): redwood routes set --policy fallback-small --force
- Verify cache: check metrics -> cache_hit_rate (>40% expected on prompt-based workflows)

Quick technical appendix (for SEs to show to infra)
- Sample API call (pseudo):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-large-quant","prompt":"...","stream":true}'
- Note: enable header X-Trace-Id for tracing across services

Notes to self (non-polished)
- Need one-pager mapping of "pilot size -> recommended pool" (Ethan to draft)
- Add a tiny spreadsheet: cost calc for g4dn vs a100 vs quantized CPU fallback
- Confirm SLA wording with legal (Priya) — particularly for Private deployments
- Link: security review template draft (CONFLUENCE-12345)

Open questions
- Is there a micro-commit SKU for 2-week pilots? (finance ask) JIRA-OPS-789
- Should we include a short AB test case example (A:dedicated B:hosted) in the slide 6?

Action items (owners)
- Draft quick spreadsheet mapping (Ethan) — due 2026-03-14
- Legal to review pilot SLA addendum (Priya) — due 2026-03-18
- Convert to slide deck + art (Noah) — deliver v0 by 2026-03-12 (we missed this, update)

End of doc. Keep short. This is a working sketch — expected to be chopped into two deliverables: 1) 8-slide SE deck, 2) 1-page battlecard PDF for quick share during calls.

-- Maya (notes)
